headline: Video generation startup PixVerse raises $439M, valuation soars past $2B
summary: Singapore-based PixVerse has closed its Series C extension, raising $439 million and pushing its valuation past $2 billion. The funds will expand its world model offering and global customer reach.
details: Singapore-based video generation startup PixVerse has closed its Series C extension, raising a total of $439 million. This new funding tranche has propelled the company's valuation past $2 billion. PixVerse aims to expand its world model offering and reach customers across various geographies.

The extension round included investments from Alibaba, Lollapalooza Capital, Ivy Capital, Grand Mount Capital, Eastern Bell Capital, Mirae Asset, BlueFocus, and CloudAlpha. Returning investors iGlobe Partners and OCBC’s LionX Ventures also participated, following an initial Series C round in March.

Founded in 2023 by Wang Changhu and Jaden Xie, PixVerse offers multiple models for video generation. These include a V-Series for consumer and API use, a C-Series for professional film, and an R-Series of world models for game development and world building.

The platform enables users to generate videos in up to 4K resolution with integrated audio. Its consumer product boasts over 150 million registered users and more than 15 million monthly active users. Image-to-video generation is offered at a competitive rate of $4.80 per minute.

PixVerse's core strength, according to Xie, lies in its data labeling methodology. Co-founder Changhu's background at ByteDance, where he built core visual understanding technology for TikTok, provides a unique advantage in accurately labeling data for high-quality video models.

The company has ambitious plans for global enterprise outreach this year, including a deal with investor Alibaba to deploy video generation features. Product rollouts include a new V-series model and an updated version of its world model.

With 150 employees across Singapore, Beijing, and Shanghai, PixVerse intends to hire more researchers and expand its go-to-market team with the new funding. The video generation market remains highly competitive, with numerous players globally.
